markdown_report:
The next experiment should isolate **terminal-loss scheduling in one BERT4Rec per category**, after repairing diagnostic category identity. At 20% progress, this remains a feasible, interpretable direction. Its user-facing benefits are hypotheses requiring validation.

**Insights and framework.** Explicit per-example reduction makes terminal/interior weighting identifiable; equal branch sizes alone do not. Electronics has weaker sampled-pair separation (p10 −0.126; negative wins 11.34%), motivating investigation without establishing a validation deficit. Missing category identity blocks serving parity everywhere: history sensitivity remains unknown, and embedding scores near 0.5 do not establish collapse.

[BERT4Rec](https://arxiv.org/abs/1904.06690) already includes last-item masking; terminal supervision is established prior art. [RSS](https://arxiv.org/abs/2207.02643) studies fixed recency-biased position sampling, removal and set prediction, rather than this loss schedule. [From Past To Path](https://arxiv.org/html/2509.23649v1) further limits novelty through reconstruction-to-prediction curricula in another model family. [Curriculum research](https://arxiv.org/abs/2012.03107) motivates fixed horizons and ordering controls.

| Direction | Mechanism | Unresolved gap |
|---|---|---|
| Objective alignment | Terminal/interior curriculum | Timing versus cumulative weighting? |
| Temporal representation | Joint time-gap attention bias; [TiSASRec](https://jiachengli1995.github.io/files/wsdm20.pdf) | Do timestamps identify current intent? |
| Ranking discrimination | Modest mined-negative fraction; [Prakash et al.](https://arxiv.org/abs/2410.17276) | Better ranking without excessive false negatives? |

**Candidate assessments.** Scores: originality/future potential/user alignment/model alignment/code difficulty; higher difficulty means harder implementation. Alignment scores describe hypotheses.

| Idea | Scores | Positive / negative assessment by criterion |
|---|---|---|
| Terminal curriculum | 3/6/5/5/4 | O: controlled timing / related curricula; F: reusable / possibly negligible; U: current-choice supervision / no compatibility reasoning; M: terminal separation / cause unknown; D: scalar change / replay and parity auditing |
| Time-gap bias | 5/7/7/4/7 | O: family adaptation / established attention; F: flexible timing / sparse timestamps; U: stale-interest hypothesis / ambiguous gaps; M: measurable sensitivity / unavailable; D: compact parameters / timestamp parity |
| Hard-negative fraction | 3/6/6/7/5 | O: simple adaptation / established method; F: sharper ranking / sampling dependence; U: plausible competitors / false negatives; M: weak margins / training-only evidence; D: unchanged backbone / mining cost |

**Selected algorithm.** Retain α(e)=0.5+0.3·min(e/100,1), separately normalized branch losses and unchanged examples. It targets stale interests outranking current preferences and unsupported broad extensions outranking precise choices; duplicate functionality remains unresolved. It also targets weak sampled separation, without assuming its cause.

Replace the primary constant control with the exact exposure-matched mean: **0.72425 for 200 epochs indexed 0–199**. Retain constants 0.5 and 0.8 as secondary anchors. Budget permitting, reverse and deterministically shuffle the same weight sequence. Match minibatches, initialization, optimizer, learning-rate schedule, updates and checkpoint rules; report coefficient and learning-rate-weighted sums. Neither matches Adam gradient exposure. Report fixed-final and identically selected checkpoints separately. Repair category identity, verify serialized serving parity, preserve all benchmark constraints, and select by host macro validation HR@10. No gain or semantic repair is established.

idea.description: Test a linear terminal-objective curriculum within corrected BERT4Rec, increasing the separately normalized terminal-prefix loss coefficient from 0.5 to 0.8 over the first 100 epochs. Compare primarily with an exposure-matched constant coefficient; use reversed and shuffled weight sequences as additional attribution controls when the shared search budget permits. Each experiment trains exactly one independent model per category and serves one selected checkpoint per category.
idea.motivation: Terminal-prefix supervision matches appended-mask inference. Increasing its contribution could address two observed user failures: stale interests outranking current preferences, and unsupported broad extensions outranking precise current choices. These are plausible mechanisms, not demonstrated semantic capabilities; terminal weighting cannot directly establish compatibility or detect duplicate functionality. Electronics' negative tenth-percentile sampled margin motivates measuring discrimination, but does not identify a scheduling problem. Missing ModelView category identity is an established diagnostic integration defect and must be repaired before interpreting serving-dependent probes. Compared with architectural alternatives, this experiment is appropriate at 20% research progress because it changes a small, identifiable part of training. Originality is modest given BERT4Rec's terminal masking and related reconstruction-to-prediction curricula.
idea.implementation_notes: Start from the supplied corrected BERT4Rec and change only branch coefficients after verifying that the baseline already uses the intended reduction. If it does not, establish the explicit-reduction baseline first; otherwise normalization and scheduling would be confounded. Keep user/endpoint sampling, negative sampling, optimizer, architecture, corruption policy and predictor writer unchanged. Average existing token losses over supervised positions within each example, then average examples within each branch. Require both branches and at least one supervised position per example. Retain terminal and interior examples every update. Apply alpha=0.5+0.3*min(epoch_index/100,1) with zero-based epochs. For a prespecified horizon T, calculate the constant control from the actual discrete schedule, not its endpoints: for T=200 and 200 updates per epoch, mean alpha=0.72425. Constants 0.5 and 0.8 remain secondary anchors and do not isolate timing. Reverse the recorded sequence or shuffle it with a dedicated seed-42 RNG; record whether permutation occurs at update or epoch resolution. Use epoch-resolution permutation here, preserving each epoch's 200 identical coefficients. Do not consume the sampler RNG when constructing controls. Preserve identical initialization, optimizer configuration and initial state, learning-rate schedule, minibatch identities, endpoint draws, masks, negative candidates, dropout RNG policy, update counts and loss reductions across trials. Deterministic replay can use separate seeded RNG streams or a recorded sampling plan; do not reuse trained checkpoints or inspect other trials. Weight schedules can be generated independently from the specification. Report sums of alpha and 1-alpha and their learning-rate-weighted sums. These do not guarantee equal gradients, gradient norms or Adam trajectories. Keep the same fixed horizon, validation cadence, checkpoint eligibility and deterministic tie-breaking rule across controls; record the host baseline's exact rules rather than inventing replacements. Retain fixed-final checkpoint results separately from identically selected best-validation checkpoint results. Each evaluation loads only its designated single checkpoint; never average checkpoints or combine scores. Host macro validation HR@10 remains the selection metric. Prioritize the schedule and exposure-matched constant; run reversed/shuffled controls and endpoint anchors only if the remaining shared 43,200 GPU-second budget supports them. Without ordering controls, limit conclusions to the comparisons actually completed. Every control includes all four categories. Use preprocessing seed 0, training seed 42, exactly 200 batches per epoch and at most 200 epochs; use the same prespecified horizon across compared runs and do not extend it after observing validation. Preserve supplied splits, pinned candidates/evaluator, category routing, single-GPU execution and DATA_DIR=os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR']; write artifacts beneath each trial directory. Terminal examples withhold their target and every later interaction before appending MASK. Interior targets remain replaced with the reserved MASK token. No shifted targets, extra datasets, pretrained weights, timestamps or metadata features are introduced. Preserve left padding and final-nonpadding MASK readout, never count-1. Keep embedded predictor and checkpoint architecture consistent. Pass the actual category into ModelView.dataset_name and retain item_emb, log2feats(sequence), predict_score(features, items), user_train, meta_data and review_data compatibility. Retain DiagnosisProbe(view, device), run_full_diagnosis(train_loader) returning metrics and metric_definitions, and diagnosis_interpreter_prompt(raw_diagnosis). Verify exact serialized weight identity and short/full-length/truncated/batched serving parity before sensitivity or residual probes. Record terminal and interior sampled-margin diagnostics separately, including counts and definitions, using the same diagnostic sampling policy across comparisons. Existing aggregate margins cannot be attributed to either branch. Do not treat training margins as validation metrics or infer history insensitivity from unavailable measurements. Known-history exclusions and sampler provenance must remain those of the supplied baseline. Uniform negatives can encourage easy discrimination and popularity shortcuts; the curriculum does not eliminate these risks. Inspect available training-frequency and history-length strata descriptively without adding independently fitted scores. Keep unavailable user-choice, incompatibility and duplicate-functionality outcomes explicitly unmeasured unless the simulator supplies them. Repeated validation selection can overfit the 200-user/category validation panel; prespecify comparisons, report all attempted outcomes and avoid schedule tuning after inspecting results. The prior combined_score=0.5425 does not establish improvement by this proposal. No executable baseline source is included in the supplied report, so the pseudocode is an integration specification rather than a standalone train.py.
idea.pseudocode:
import numpy as np

# Prespecify the same horizon for every compared experiment.
EPOCHS = 200
BATCHES_PER_EPOCH = 200
base = np.array([0.5 + 0.3 * min(e / 100.0, 1.0)
                 for e in range(EPOCHS)], dtype=np.float64)
mean_alpha = float(base.mean())  # 0.72425 at EPOCHS=200

# Generate schedules locally from the specification; never load another trial.
# Dedicated RNG prevents changing training samples or initialization.
permutation = np.random.default_rng(42).permutation(EPOCHS)
schedules = {
    'forward': base,
    'exposure_matched_constant': np.full(EPOCHS, mean_alpha),
    'reversed': base[::-1].copy(),
    'shuffled_epochs': base[permutation],
    'constant_0.5': np.full(EPOCHS, 0.5),
    'constant_0.8': np.full(EPOCHS, 0.8),
}

# Run ONE selected schedule per independent trial; controls are never fused.
weights = schedules[trial_schedule_name]

def branch_mean(token_loss, supervised):
    count = supervised.sum(dim=1)
    assert bool((count > 0).all())
    masked_loss = token_loss.masked_fill(~supervised.bool(), 0.0)
    return (masked_loss.sum(dim=1) / count).mean()

for category in FOUR_SUPPLIED_CATEGORIES:
    model, optimizer = initialize_supplied_baseline(category, training_seed=42)
    sampler = supplied_sampler_with_reproducible_rng_streams(category)
    coefficient_sums = np.zeros(2)
    lr_weighted_sums = np.zeros(2)
    for epoch in range(EPOCHS):
        for batch_index in range(BATCHES_PER_EPOCH):
            terminal, interior = sampler.next_branches()
            # Terminal: target and later events absent; appended reserved MASK.
            # Interior: every supervised target replaced by reserved MASK.
            Lt = branch_mean(existing_token_loss(model, terminal), terminal.supervised)
            Li = branch_mean(existing_token_loss(model, interior), interior.supervised)
            alpha = float(weights[epoch])
            loss = alpha * Lt + (1.0 - alpha) * Li
            optimizer.zero_grad()
            loss.backward()
            # Preserve all baseline clipping, regularization and LR step rules.
            lr = current_baseline_learning_rate(optimizer)
            optimizer.step()
            apply_unchanged_baseline_scheduler_step_if_due()
            coefficient_sums += [alpha, 1.0 - alpha]
            lr_weighted_sums += lr * np.array([alpha, 1.0 - alpha])
        run_unchanged_validation_and_checkpoint_selection()
    record_fixed_final_and_selected_checkpoint_results_separately()
    export_matching_predictor_and_one_designated_checkpoint(category)
    view = supplied_ModelView(model=model, dataset_name=category)
    verify_exact_checkpoint_identity_and_complete_serving_parity(view)
    # Sensitivity/residual probes remain unavailable unless their gates pass.
    record_coefficient_exposure_and_branch_diagnostics()

# Serving remains unchanged: observed history -> truncate to maxlen-1 ->
# append MASK -> left-pad -> bidirectional BERT4Rec -> final nonpadding MASK.
# Host independently evaluates its pinned four-category macro validation HR@10.
# Never fuse categories, trials, checkpoints, or independently fitted scores.

originality.positive: The specific interpolation and exposure-matched ordering controls define a precise BERT4Rec experiment distinct from fixed terminal masking or fixed recency sampling.
originality.negative: Terminal masking, multi-objective weighting and reconstruction-to-prediction curricula have prior art; novelty of this exact schedule is unestablished.

future_potential.positive: A reproducible timing effect could inform how one BERT4Rec balances bidirectional reconstruction and terminal recommendation with little architectural complexity.
future_potential.negative: Benefits may be explained by average weighting, optimizer interactions or checkpoint selection, and may not address compatibility or duplicate functionality.

code_difficulty.positive: The architecture and predictor remain unchanged, and schedule generation requires little code.
code_difficulty.negative: Faithful attribution requires reduction auditing, reproducible sampling, controlled schedule replay, checkpoint reporting and repaired serving-parity integration; the supplied material lacks executable baseline code.

related_work.title: BERT4Rec: Sequential Recommendation with Bidirectional Encoder Representations from Transformer
contributions: Establishes bidirectional masked-item recommendation with reserved MASK tokens and appended-mask inference.
Includes last-item-only masking samples to address the training/inference mismatch; terminal masking is established prior art.
limitations: Does not specify or validate the proposed epoch-dependent terminal/interior interpolation.
The original full-catalog likelihood differs from a supplied baseline using sampled losses; preserve the baseline objective when isolating scheduling.

related_work.title: Recency-based Sampling of Sequences for Sequential Recommendation
contributions: Investigates fixed recency-biased position sampling, motivating attention to the relationship between training targets and terminal recommendation.
Samples positions with replacement, collapses duplicate selections, removes selected items and predicts their positive set using sequence-level objectives.
limitations: Does not evaluate a temporal loss-weight curriculum or use the proposed BERT4Rec branch interpolation.
Its removal, set-prediction and negative-sampling procedures should not be substituted into this controlled experiment.

related_work.title: Time Interval Aware Self-Attention for Sequential Recommendation
contributions: Models pairwise time intervals alongside positional information, motivating the temporal-representation alternative.
limitations: Uses a different backbone; a BERT4Rec adaptation requires separate implementation and inference timestamp parity.
Does not establish that recent interactions should dominate or that time gaps identify current intent.

related_work.title: Prakash et al. (2024): negative-sampling comparison referenced in the supplied search results
contributions: Compares negative-sampling strategies and motivates treating effectiveness and popularity-band effects as dataset dependent.
limitations: Does not establish that model-mined negatives improve this benchmark.
Unobserved candidates can be false negatives; better sampled margins alone do not establish better HR@10.

related_work.title: Curriculum Learning by Transfer Learning: Theory and Experiments with Deep Networks
contributions: Supports examining curriculum ordering against alternative orders while controlling pacing.
limitations: Does not establish the proposed terminal/interior loss schedule or a universal exposure-matching protocol for recommendation.

related_work.title: When Do Curricula Work?
contributions: Motivates evaluating curriculum benefits under an explicitly fixed training budget.
limitations: Does not demonstrate benefits for the pinned Amazon categories or the proposed BERT4Rec objective.

related_work.title: Random Weighting for Multi-Task Learning
contributions: Shows that random loss weighting can be competitive, motivating stronger controls than equal weights alone.
limitations: Does not directly evaluate these two BERT4Rec branches.
Replaying a shuffled coefficient sequence is an attribution control proposed here, rather than an experimentally established consequence of this work.

related_work.title: From Past To Path (2025)
contributions: Studies joint history reconstruction and next-item training with decreasing masking and a final next-item-only phase.
Provides related prior art for reconstruction-to-prediction curricula.
limitations: Uses semantic-ID generative models and equal loss weights, rather than this BERT4Rec interpolation.
Does not validate the proposed schedule or eliminate the need for exposure-matched and ordering controls.
